lessonRef.unitTitle: PF1 — Earning Income: Income, Benefits, and the Cost of Getting Qualified
lessonRef.title: Concept model B: payroll deductions a worker is likely to see

focus: payroll deductions a worker is likely to see
objective: Read each line of a fictional pay stub, compute the five separate deductions a first-time worker is likely to see, and total them against net pay.
scenario: This is a fictional pay stub for Marcus Adeyemi, a made-up lifeguard at a simulated municipal pool. The employer, the amounts, and the tax rates are all invented for practice.
safetyNotes: Every figure, person, employer, institution, offer, account, and document on this task sheet is fictional and exists only for practice.
No real transaction is part of this lesson, and no real bank, card, brokerage, tax, or login detail is ever requested. If a task sheet ever appears to ask for one, stop and tell a trusted adult.
This lesson teaches general financial concepts and does not advise anyone about their own money. For a real decision, talk with a trusted adult or a qualified licensed professional.
materials: the fictional pay-stub lines in these directions

tasks.directions: Marcus’s fictional stub shows gross pay of $612.00 for the period. Social Security is withheld at 6.2% of gross and Medicare at 1.45% of gross. Round each deduction to the nearest cent.

prompts.text: How much is withheld for Social Security?
How much is withheld for Medicare?

tasks.directions: The same stub also shows state income tax at 4.25% of gross, a city income tax at 1% of gross, and federal income tax withheld of $38.50.

prompts.text: How much is withheld for state income tax?
How much is withheld for city income tax?
What is the total of all five deductions on the stub?
What is Marcus’s net pay for the period?
What percentage of gross pay was withheld in total? Round to one decimal place.
Two of the five deductions on Marcus’s stub are not income tax at all. Name them and say what they pay for.

remediation: Use the fictional scenario and work one graded prompt at a time. For each number response, copy the given fictional quantities into integer cents, choose the operation the wording calls for, calculate, and check the result with an inverse operation or estimate. For each written response, make a claim and support it with at least one detail from the fictional scenario. Use these steps to check the method while keeping every final result in your own response.
extension: Marcus picks up a second fictional shift and his gross rises to $748.00. Recompute all four percentage deductions and state which stub line stays fixed.
